children: Deepinder Goyal’s health-tech venture Temple has partnered with the Sri Sri Institute for Advanced Research (SSIAR), the research arm of Art of Living, to study how different meditation practices affect the body’s parasympathetic response.

Goyal, founder of Eternal and Zomato, said the collaboration will use Entropy, a biomarker on Temple that tracks the body’s sympathetic and parasympathetic state, to measure the effects of different meditation practices in real time.
“Entropy is a new biomarker on Temple that also measures your body’s (para)sympathetic state, and we have seen it drop real time during meditation, while HR stays flat,” Goyal said in a post.

The study will involve experienced meditators at the Art of Living ashram, with Temple measuring changes in Entropy during different meditation practices. Goyal said the objective is to determine which practices produce the strongest parasympathetic response.
“I am looking forward to seeing which meditation practice produces the deepest parasympathetic response,” he said.

Goyal said he visited Art of Living as part of the research after seeking to involve Gurudev, who declined to participate personally but suggested that the study be conducted with experienced meditators at the ashram.

Describing Temple as a “science first organisation”, Goyal said the collaboration is focused on measuring meditation’s impact through Entropy. He added that the results of the studies with Art of Living will be published soon.

The collaboration follows Goyal’s recent posts about using Entropy to track changes in his own recovery during meditation. According to Goyal, the metric allowed him to observe changes in recovery minute by minute even when his heart rate remained relatively unchanged.

Temple positions Entropy as a metric for tracking physiological changes that may not be immediately apparent through conventional heart-rate monitoring. The latest study with Art of Living is expected to provide comparative data on how different meditation practices influence the body’s parasympathetic response.
